narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed by our credit model, which looks at various aspects of your financial profile to assess risk, drawing from historical data on borrowers in 1970s Germany. With your checking account showing a negative balance under 0 DM, a requested loan duration of 42 months—much longer than the 19-month average for approved applicants—and a credit history marked as critical with other existing credits, the model identified several concerns that led to its decision. It calculated a 58% probability that you represent a bad credit risk, meaning it predicted a higher-than-even chance of challenges repaying the loan, which is why your application for 3394 DM to cover repairs was denied.

The two strongest factors pushing toward this unfavorable prediction were your checking account status and the lengthy loan duration you requested. A negative balance stands out as a major red flag, since only about 20% of approved applicants had this, compared to over half with no account issues, signaling to the model potential ongoing cash flow problems. Similarly, your 42-month term is more than double the typical approved duration, which often correlates with higher default risks in past cases, as longer commitments strain repayment ability.

On a more positive note, your credit history, while critical, had the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward approval—it's a factor that sometimes offsets other issues for those who've managed payments despite past hiccups, unlike the majority of approved applicants who had fully paid credits. These top three elements—your account status, loan length, and credit background—together outweighed other details like your unemployed status, car property, or own housing, which are more common among approved borrowers but weren't decisive here.

Compared to typical approved applicants, who often have shorter loans, healthier checking accounts, and steadier employment like 1-4 years on the job, your profile aligns more closely with higher-risk patterns the model has learned to flag. Your age of 65, lack of telephone, and job as unemployed/unskilled non-resident also didn't help, though they played smaller roles.

To improve your chances next time, consider shortening the loan term, building up your checking account balance, and demonstrating improved credit management—perhaps by paying down existing credits or providing additional guarantors beyond your co-applicant setup. We recommend reapplying after addressing these, or consulting a financial advisor to strengthen your overall stability.
